summary: Some deployments, such as Lightweight 4over6, need a client to hold a whole range of ports instead of just one. This standards-track RFC extends the Port Control Protocol with a new PORT_SET option on the MAP operation, letting a client request and manage a set of ports as a single unit.

eli5.summary: Instead of asking for one parking space at a time, you can ask for a whole row of spaces in one go.

questions: how to request multiple ports with pcp
what does the pcp parity bit do
subtitle: One PCP request that reserves a whole range of ports instead of a single port.

tldr.problem: The Port Control Protocol maps one port per MAP request, but some uses, such as Lightweight 4over6 or a SIP server handling many calls, need a whole set of ports.
tldr.mechanism: A new MAP option, PORT_SET (option number 130), carries the number of ports wanted and the first internal port, so the server can map the whole range as one unit.
tldr.outcome: Clients save signaling, latency and server state, and the server may still grant fewer ports than asked for. Renewal and deletion also treat the set as a single entity.

today: RFC 7753 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends PCP as defined in RFC 6887.

sections.title: Why Ask for a Set of Ports
sections.content:
RFC 7753 extends the Port Control Protocol (PCP, RFC 6887) so that a client can retrieve a set of ports with a single request. It does this by defining one new option, PORT_SET, for the MAP opcode.

The RFC lists several use cases. A SIP User Agent Server that expects many concurrent calls needs media ports, and sending a separate MAP request for each one during call setup would add latency and signaling load. It can instead pre-allocate a set of ports so that no PCP exchange is needed when a call arrives. Port ranges are also common in firewall rules, for example for RTP traffic.

The extension is generic and is expected to be useful for other cases as well.
sections.eli5: Some programs need lots of mailboxes at once. Asking for them all together is faster than asking one at a time.

sections.title: The Need for PORT_SET
sections.content:
Several plain MAP requests can reach roughly the same result as one request with a PORT_SET option. The RFC argues that PORT_SET is better on four counts.

  • Network traffic: one request uses fewer network resources than many.
  • Latency: even when requests are sent in parallel, total processing time is expected to be longer for many requests than for one.
  • Server-side efficiency: some devices, for example a carrier-grade NAT using a bulk port allocation scheme, process port sets much more efficiently than individual ports.
  • Server-side scalability: the number of state table entries is often a limiting factor, and a whole set can use a single mapping entry.

PORT_SET also supports parity preservation. Some protocols, such as RTP, give meaning to whether a port number is even or odd, so the mapping may need to keep that property.
sections.eli5: One big order is cheaper and quicker than many little ones. Some games need even-numbered and odd-numbered seats kept in the right places, and this lets you ask for that.

sections.title: The PORT_SET Option Format
sections.content:
PORT_SET has option number 130, is valid only for the MAP opcode, has a length of 5 bytes, may appear in both requests and responses, and may occur at most once. Two PORT_SET options would imply two overlapping Suggested External Port Sets, which is why the limit is one.

The option has these fields:

  • Port Set Size: a 16-bit unsigned integer, the number of ports requested. It MUST NOT be zero.
  • First Internal Port: in a request, the client MUST set it equal to the Internal Port field in the MAP opcode. In a response, it gives the first internal port of the set the server mapped, which may differ from what was sent.
  • P (parity bit): 1 if parity preservation is requested, 0 otherwise.
  • Reserved: MUST be zero when sending and ignored when receiving.

The Internal, Suggested External and Assigned External Port Sets are each the range of Port Set Size ports starting at the relevant first port. The option number is in the optional-to-process range (128-191), so a server that does not know PORT_SET treats the request as an ordinary single-port MAP request.
sections.eli5: The request says how many ports you want, where your range starts, and whether you need odd and even numbers kept lined up. A server that has never heard of the idea just gives you one port.

sections.title: Client and Server Behavior
sections.content:
To get a set, the client adds a PORT_SET option to its MAP request. It MUST NOT include more than one; if it needs several sets it sends separate MAP requests with distinct Internal Ports. A client that does not know how many ports it needs MAY set Port Set Size to 0xffff to accept as many as the server can offer. It SHOULD NOT send PORT_SET for single-port requests, and PREFER_FAILURE MUST NOT appear in a request with PORT_SET.

A server handling a PORT_SET option with a non-zero Requested Lifetime returns MALFORMED_OPTION if there are several PORT_SET options, if Port Set Size is zero, or if PREFER_FAILURE is present. The server MAY map fewer ports than requested but MUST NOT map more, and it SHOULD map as many as possible and at least one. If it ends up mapping only one port, the response MUST NOT contain a PORT_SET option.

If the parity bit is set, the server MAY preserve parity, in which case the External Port has the same parity as the First Internal Port. On success, the Assigned External Port is the first port of the external set and Port Set Size is the number of ports actually mapped.
sections.eli5: You ask once for your row of spaces. The manager may give you a shorter row, but never a longer one, and if you get only one space the answer looks like a normal single-space answer.

sections.title: Discovery, Renewal, Deletion and Overlap
sections.content:
If a response has no PORT_SET option, the client cannot conclude that the server lacks support, because the server may simply have chosen to allocate one port. A server that gains or loses port-set capability while running MAY reset its Epoch time and send an ANNOUNCE message, which makes clients retry.

A port-set mapping is renewed and deleted as a single entity: the lifetime of every mapping in the set is set to the Assigned Lifetime at once. A client refreshing or deleting a set MUST include the PORT_SET option.

A request, with or without PORT_SET, that tries to map Internal Ports already covered by existing mappings is treated as a refresh. Each matching single-port or port-set mapping is processed independently, as if a separate refresh had arrived, and the server sends a Mapping Update message for each. Because the outcome of overlapping requests depends on the order in which the server receives them, clients MUST ensure their port-set requests do not inadvertently overlap.
sections.eli5: Renewing or giving back the row happens for the whole row at once. If you accidentally ask for spaces you already own, the manager just treats it as a renewal.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
In the first example an application wants 100 IPv4 UDP ports starting at 50,000 and does not care which external ports it gets. The server is configured by local policy to allocate only 32 ports per user, so it maps external UDP ports 37,056 to 37,087 on 192.0.2.3 to internal ports 50,000 to 50,031 and replies with Port Set Size 32. The host decides 32 is enough, closes its sockets for ports 50,032 to 50,099 and starts a refresh timer.

In the second example a host discovers a stateless NAT44 mapping by requesting Port Set Size 65,535 from internal port 1. The server replies with a 2048-port set starting at port 26,624 on 192.0.2.5.

In the third example, internal port 100 is mapped to external port 100 and the set 101-199 is mapped to 201-299. A request for a set of 100 ports from port 100 with the same nonce is treated as two refreshes, and the server sends two responses.
sections.eli5: A program asks for 100 spaces, is given 32, and happily hands back the ones it cannot use.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content:
The server decides any port-set quota per client. If it gives one subscriber several port sets, it SHOULD assign the same external IP address in each response. To keep the number of mapping entries down, the RFC recommends configuring the server to assign the maximum allowed Port Set Size in a single response, and this policy SHOULD be configurable. The failover mechanism of RFC 6887 also applies to port sets.

PCP is idempotent, and PORT_SET keeps that property with one caveat: the order in which overlapping requests arrive affects the mappings created. For example, with request A for ports 1-10 and request B for ports 5-14, receiving A first makes B a refresh of A's mapping, while the reverse order produces a different mapping. One suggested way to avoid this is a central PCP client process on the host, or acquiring ports from the operating system with bind() before mapping them.

When a client gets fewer ports than it asked for, the RFC leaves the response to the implementation. The client cannot know why the server gave fewer ports, some clients work fine with fewer, and asking for more could be seen as abuse. The RFC expects that for most applications asking for more would not be worth the cost.
sections.eli5: Do not ask for overlapping rows, because the answer depends on which request the manager reads first. If you get a shorter row than you hoped, it usually is not worth pestering the manager.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 6887 apply. One new concern is that a single PORT_SET request can produce several responses when its nonce matches several mappings. An on-path attacker who eavesdrops a nonce could use that for an amplification attack. Using PCP authentication eliminates this attack vector. To stop one client from taking all ports on a shared IP address, port quotas should be configured on the server.

IANA allocated value 130 in the "PCP Options" registry for PORT_SET.
sections.eli5: Someone listening in could trick the manager into sending many replies at once, so use the secret handshake. Also keep one customer from grabbing all the spaces.

fields.desc: Equals the MAP Internal Port in a request; first port of the mapped set in a response.
